statement: In a town with square blocks, Omar walks 3 blocks north, then 4 blocks east, then 3 blocks south. How many blocks is he from where he started?

choices.misconception: I thought going north and then south brings him back to the start, and forgot the blocks he walked east.
I thought he ends up as far away as the last part of his walk.
I added the 3 blocks north and the 4 blocks east and forgot he walked back south.
I added up every block he walked, not how far he is from the start.

hints: Draw his walk on squared paper.
Draw each part of the walk as an arrow. Walking north and then the same distance south cancels out, so look at what is left.
The 3 blocks north and the 3 blocks south cancel. Only the walk east is left.

solutions.reliable: Draw it. Going 3 blocks north and later 3 blocks south brings him back to the same street he started on. He is still 4 blocks east of the start, so he is 4 blocks away. The idea to keep: draw the path, then compare where it ends with where it began.
solutions.elegant: North and south cancel when they are the same length, so only the east part counts: 4 blocks.

whyOnTest: Distance from the start differs from distance walked, and a quick sketch makes the difference obvious.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
